title: Biagini's background and Artie Shaw approaches the sidemen
summary: Biagini came from the Detroit Graystone ballroom; during a Roseland matinee Artie Shaw asks Leeman, Best and Robinson to join his new band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And who was this Hank Biagmini Veogene?
He worked in that Detroit ballroom in that band. (Casa Loma Band's predecessor - a Jean Goldkette unit called 'The Orange Blossoms'.)
The Grey Stone Ballroom. And he conducted. He was a --
He was a non-competitive trumpet player, but a leader.

Yes. A haphazard name for having a steppingstone, as Joe Haymes' orchestra was later on -- it was a steppingstone for good musicians. Anyway, on a Sunday afternoon, somebody said, 'Somebody here wants to talk to you' and we were at the Roseland doing a matinee, the old Roseland on Broadway. The other band across from us was Woody Herman, his first three weeks that he broke up with Isham Jones, and were forming a new orchestra. I was with Hank Biagmini Viagmini.
And we were performing in the afternoon, a Sunday matinee, and somebody said that Artie Shaw would like to meet me, if you've ever heard of him.
